findings.title: The "ask" handoff branch deletes trial answers without asking
findings.problem: When guestHandoff returns "ask", this branch immediately clears both trial copies and shows "Welcome back." No Add/Discard choice exists. This contradicts the documented handoff and the sign-in screen's promise to add the trial to the account. The browser tests titled "asks first" and "Add merges once" actually assert that the existing log remains unchanged and the trial is deleted, so they certify the wrong behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A visitor completes five trial questions and signs into an older account. Their trial answers are permanently removed without consent or a successful merged save. An older account with no saved progress is affected too.
findings.fix: Preserve the trial while presenting the documented Add/Discard choice. Implement a bounded, idempotent merge for consenting returning accounts, retaining their existing progress. Clear the trial only after explicit Discard or a successful save containing the merge. Make the browser tests click both choices and verify their different outcomes.

findings.title: The skip fallback reopens deferred unresolved reviews
findings.problem: Leaving an unresolved review adds its identity to the deferred set, but also leaves a skipped entry in the navigation history. When sessionPool has no eligible questions, fallbackSkip(trail) ignores the deferred set and selects that same entry. reveal then restores the remembered unresolved card.
findings.failure_scenario: A student's bank is otherwise exhausted and Today contains only an unresolved due miss. Tapping "Leave unresolved" repeatedly returns to the same card instead of ending the round. The existing browser test avoids this failure by supplying fresh questions.
findings.fix: Exclude deferred unresolved identities from the navigation fallback as well as the question pool. Finish the automatic round when only deferred entries remain, while preserving fallback behavior for ordinary skipped questions. Add a browser test with an unresolved review and an empty fresh pool.

findings.title: Legacy resolution ignores rows that have not yet been classified
findings.problem: The choice handler updates only rows with row.unclassified set. Legacy saves initially contain unscoped rows without that flag, and classifyLog does not run until both catalog reads succeed. QBank nevertheless generates unresolved-choice cards for ambiguous unscoped misses. Choosing a candidate therefore moves the schedule but leaves those log rows unresolved.
findings.failure_scenario: The question-bank query succeeds while the case-study query fails or remains pending. A legacy miss shares an ID between a bank question and a bundled question. The student identifies the question, but the log receives no canonical identity, so the unresolved review returns and the chosen question can receive first-try XP rather than correction XP.
findings.fix: Resolve eligible rows that lack a canonical identity, including both explicitly unclassified rows and untouched unscoped legacy rows. Do not rewrite already classified rows. Add an integration test where the bank read succeeds, the case read fails, and choosing a candidate removes the unresolved review and preserves correction behavior.

assessment: Do not ship. The returning-account handoff silently deletes trial answers, and two legacy-review paths can leave students unable to clear a review. The handoff tests also assert the discard behavior instead of exercising their advertised Add/Discard flow. Review was based on the supplied code and images; tests were not run.
